review: Request: Wren asked to extend her mastered sectional hand-twisting method beyond its 0.60 m requested-length ceiling, making one continuous two-ply reed cord in successive hand-sized sections without joining cords; her real 0.64 m cord was assessed at tick 367 as needing 0.8911 m for one frapping turn on her two-turn right-angle lashing. The World Agent decided develop (learning 1): the minimal general extension of hand-twist-sectioned-cord@1 that removes only the arbitrary ceiling while keeping strand length, conserved volume, 1-12 mm plies, condition, dry footing and working space, with no duplicated material, sampling, trial or cord mechanics, no splicing or joining, and no inference that about 1.0 m is feasible. Implemented hand-twist-long-sectioned-cord@1 as a simplified but real mechanism, not a first release, because the specification is self-consistent and implementable: modes sample, make, inspect, trial and cancel. make reserves 0.2-1 unit of one sampled fiber and source atomically through the existing escrow, then runs N = ceil(L/0.30) sections of three paid 1-energy rounds (separate-align or regrip, twist, counter-ply) and one paid release check through the existing paid-work helper, 3N+1 rounds and energy in all (7 at 0.60 m, 13 at 1.0 m); round 1 measures intact fiber, sets broken strands aside as owned scrap and either aligns the first section or ends in the inherited measured shortfall that returns every reserved tenth once; only a passed release check turns the workpiece into an ordinary owned untested fiber-cord@1 cord with measured length, overall length with loose ends, ply diameter, condition and per-section endpoints. Sample, inspect and trial delegate to the existing implementations (one round each at 0.5, 0.2 and 0.5 energy). Work that is unworked, low on energy or crowded pauses uncharged; resume is make with workId only and re-measures nothing; cancel is free and death leaves the fiber where the person died, each releasing unworked fiber exactly once and refunding nothing paid. Events: long-sectioned-cord-started, -progress (with section geometry, held and plied extents and the measured feasible length range), -shortfall, -paused, -resumed, -failed, -completed, -check-failed, -cancelled, -inspected, -sampled, -trial and -broken, carrying the inherited fiber-cord visual metadata; no visual component is added. Derived upper limit, not a chosen range: no strand is spliced, so each ply (L x 2/sqrt(3) + 0.04 m) must fit in one stem; for reed (1.8 m) L <= (1.8 - 0.04) x cos 30 deg = 1.5242 m, hence at most 6 sections, 19 paid rounds and 19 energy, and a work circle of at most the actor radius + 0.9 m plus the other person's radius; the 0.2-1 unit material range is unchanged, and within it the 1 mm ply floor never binds for reed up to that length (thinnest ply 1.88 mm). Requests above it, uncovered or mixed material, too little or too much material, plies under 1 mm, crowding, low energy and irrelevant arguments are refused before any reservation or cost. Modeling assumptions: the requested-length range is the inherited 0.05 m minimum with no maximum, so the existing strand, volume and ply checks decide admissibility; one section stays the inherited 0.30 m two-hand span; regrip, twist and release need the inherited condition 0.5; the inherited 0.0005 per-round wear of every fiber-cord item applies once through hand-twist-fiber-cord@1 and none is added; study takes one round at 0.2 energy and requires individual mastery of hand-twist-sectioned-cord, which Wren has; reserved fiber stays in the owner's hands as before; the result grants no strength, frapping fit, knot, lashing, reward, satisfaction or mastery, and every consumer measures its own need (in a test fixture a 1.0 m cord from 0.2 unit was only assessed by frapping on fixture branches, not assumed to fit Wren's crossing). Reuse and choice: hand-twist-sectioned-cord@1 is installed and replays from earlier rounds, so instead of a rewriting @2 or a duplicated state machine, long-sectioned-fiber-cord.ts now passes an operation profile (ability id, revision, state key, event prefix, requested-length range) into its otherwise unchanged functions and appends a SECTIONED_CORD_WORK export; hand-twist-sectioned-cord@1 passes its own profile, so its ability text, events, records and behavior stay byte-identical (checked by its full tests, a step-by-step world-hash comparison before and after the change, and a read-only re-step of every retained ex16 replay segment), while the new package runs the same functions under its own identity and reuses the fiber-cord@1 strand law, geometry, samples, allocations, trial and wear through FIBER_CORD and FIBER_CORD_SECTIONING. Knot, join, binding, lashing and frapping accept the new cords unchanged as ordinary fiber-cord@1 cords.
